THE_SCOPE_NARROWING_THIS_LANE_MEASURED.the_gap: ANY Commercial V1 ROLE is a strictly broader predicate than SERVING A CURRENT COMMERCIAL V1 CUSTOM DOMAIN. A project can hold a Commercial V1 role while serving no custom domain at all: by holding Commercial V1 environment variables or secrets, by being bound to a Commercial V1 Supabase project or any other Commercial V1 backing service, by serving a Commercial V1 surface on a vercel.app or preview domain rather than a custom one, by holding a Commercial V1 Git integration to this same repository, by being the target of a Commercial V1 alias that is not currently attached, or by being a dormant project whose configuration would make it a Commercial V1 surface the moment a domain were attached.

Attachment is one of the cheapest and least-governed acts on the platform. A finding scoped to it can be falsified by a single alias change that no repository gate observes, which is the parent's C-6 finding applied to this specific unknown.

rollback_and_delete_rule.when_the_inverse_is_applied: Immediately, and once, if any limb of verification fails. Per the parent's adjudication P: if verification fails, apply the recorded inverse immediately and STOP; do not attempt a second variant of the mutation in the same sitting.
rollback_and_delete_rule.the_delete_is_conditional_and_bounded: The inverse deletes the ref ONLY IF verification established that this act created it. If the prestate found the ref ABSENT and verification finds it PRESENT at an UNEXPECTED SHA, the ref may have been created by another party between the two reads. In that case the correct response is STOP_UNEXPECTED_REF_STATE and a GOVERNANCE INCIDENT record, NOT a delete: deleting a ref this act did not create would destroy another party's work.
rollback_and_delete_rule.what_the_delete_does_not_restore: Nothing else needs restoring, because M-8 changes exactly one ref. This is stated so the rollback is not read as broader than it is.
rollback_and_delete_rule.irreversibility_assessment: M-8 has a CLEAN INVERSE, unlike M-5. Creating and deleting a ref leaves the commit graph unchanged, because the ref points at a commit that already existed. The one residue is that the ref name may have been fetched, cached or referenced by a third party in the interval, which is a visibility residue and not a state residue. It is recorded because the programme has measured that treating an act as reversible is the error that makes it dangerous.

retry_and_idempotence.idempotence_rule: M-8 is IDEMPOTENT ON ITS POSTCONDITION, NOT ON ITS ACT. If a re-run finds refs/heads/release/commercial-v1 already present AND at exactly the SHA this act's own record says it created, the postcondition already holds and the correct response is to CLOSE the act as ALREADY_SATISFIED, recording that no second create was performed. It is NOT to create again, and it is NOT to force-update.
retry_and_idempotence.the_case_that_is_not_idempotent: If the ref is present at a DIFFERENT SHA than this act's record names, the postcondition does NOT hold and the act is NOT re-runnable. Force-updating the ref would rewrite a branch pointer that some other act or party set. Response: STOP_UNEXPECTED_REF_STATE and a GOVERNANCE INCIDENT record.
retry_and_idempotence.retry_ceiling: AT MOST ONE retry of M-8, and only where the first attempt failed WITHOUT creating the ref, verified by a fresh read showing the ref still ABSENT. A retry after a create that partially succeeded is not a retry; it is the unexpected-ref-state case.
retry_and_idempotence.retry_requires_fresh_confirmation: A retry requires a NEW confirmation. Per adjudication Q, confirmation does not transfer to a retry.
retry_and_idempotence.retry_requires_fresh_prestate: A retry re-captures the whole prestate, including the source ref's head SHA. If the source head has advanced between the failed attempt and the retry, the retry is creating the branch at a DIFFERENT commit than the attempt the owner confirmed. That is not a retry of the confirmed act. It is a new act requiring a new confirmation stating the new SHA.
retry_and_idempotence.relationship_to_the_deployment_retry_con: M-8 is a GIT-PLANE act and is NOT governed by v1.0.2's AIC-8/AIC-9 bounded-retry chain, which governs DEPLOYMENT-creation acts under PR201's BOUNDED_RETRY_RULE. The nonce-chaining mechanism does not apply, because a git ref creation is idempotent on its postcondition in a way a deployment creation is not: a ref has a name the governing party controls, so it needs no nonce to be identifiable before it exists. This distinction is stated so no successor imports the deployment retry machinery into the git plane, or vice versa.

The absence of refs/heads/release/*, which another party could create.
The repository's ruleset set, which is hosted, mutable, and invisible to every repository gate per the parent's C-6.
fail_closed_stale_prestate_rule.why_ABANDONED_and_not_FAILED: The distinction is imported deliberately from v1.0.2's CONFIRMATION_AND_SHA_REVERIFICATION_ORDER_CORRECTION step 5, which closes a stale-SHA stop as ABANDONED rather than as a failed attempt eligible for the retry chain, on the ground that the byte-identical-SHA condition was never reached. OD4_SEQUENCE_RIDER_MACHINE_VERIFIABLE.why_it_needs_translating: As ratified it is a prohibition on a STATE OF AFFAIRS (a required check the SHA cannot produce). A prohibition on a state of affairs is verifiable only if the state is computable. The translation below makes it computable from two inputs a lane already has: the workflow corpus at a SHA, and the required-check configuration of a ref.

definitions: C = the eight required check names, from ADJUDICATIONS.D.required_checks, by exact string.
R = a ref that O-1 places under protection, or that RBD-2 extends O-1 to.

S(R) = the SHA that R's protection configuration causes GitHub to evaluate required checks against. For a pull-request gate this is the PR's evaluated SHA; for a push-evaluated gate this is the pushed commit.

PRODUCIBLE(c, S(R)) = TRUE iff the workflow corpus at that SHA contains a job whose name value equals c exactly, in a workflow whose on: triggers include an event that fires for S(R) on R, including that event's branch filter.
the_computable_predicate.RIDER_PRE_1: For every c in C configured as REQUIRED on R: PRODUCIBLE(c, S(R)) MUST be TRUE. If any is FALSE, configuring it violates the rider and the act STOPS with STOP_RIDER_VIOLATION.
the_computable_predicate.RIDER_PRE_2: O-2 is DISCHARGEABLE on R only when RIDER_PRE_1 holds for all eight. Where it holds for a proper subset, O-2 is PARTIALLY configurable: the producible subset may be required and the rest may not, and O-2 is recorded as NOT YET SATISFIED on R rather than as satisfied by the subset. A partially configured O-2 must never be reported as O-2 met.
the_computable_predicate.RIDER_PRE_3: O-3 / E is the act that makes the push-evaluated limb producible. Until E is implemented, RIDER_PRE_1 is satisfiable only on the pull-request-evaluated limb. The rider therefore does not merely SEQUENCE O-2 after O-3; for the push limb it makes O-2 UNREACHABLE until O-3 exists, which is a stronger statement than sequencing and is the reason the owner's rider was necessary rather than merely prudent.

The nonce is not unforgeable because of any platform property; it is unforgeable because it was recorded before the fact.

the_four_requirements_the_mission_names.clause: AIC-3, with AIC-2 as the carriage mechanism
the_four_requirements_the_mission_names.carried_as: The nonce and frozen SHA are passed as deployment metadata under the exact keys uellix_governed_act_nonce and uellix_governed_act_sha. The server-generated deployment id returned by the create act is captured immediately, within the same governed act, and written into the act record against the nonce. An act whose id was never bound is INCOMPLETE and its deployment is INADMISSIBLE. The deployment id is never required to pre-exist its deployment.

An act nonce binds to EXACTLY ONE deployment id: the first bound under AIC-3. Any later deployment bearing the same nonce with a different id is INADMISSIBLE as governed evidence and is a GOVERNANCE INCIDENT to be recorded rather than resolved by choosing between them. Its measured necessity is the redeploy-copy hazard: a redeploy COPIES meta, so a nonce alone does not identify one deployment. Any prestate limb, re-derived immediately before a mutation, differs from the value captured at confirmation -> the act STOPS and is closed as ABANDONED, not as a failed attempt. The retry ceiling is not consumed.
A prestate capture fails or is partial -> the mutation is not executed, because it has no rollback.
Confirmation is absent, ambiguous, or differently scoped than the act -> the act is not executed. Silence is not consent, and confirmation does not transfer to a retry, a variant, or the next act.
Verification of a mutation fails -> apply the recorded inverse immediately and STOP. Do not attempt a second variant in the same sitting.
A retry-of-a-retry is requested on the deployment path -> REFUSED at the act-record stage, without re-evaluating BR-1..BR-5, per AIC-9.
The retry identity chain is to be cited as EVIDENCE and EXEC-NOTE-1 is undischarged -> STOP. The chain may be kept as an internal discipline; it may not be cited as proof.
This artifact and PR201 could be read to conflict -> PR201 CONTROLS and the consumer STOPS.

This artifact and the frozen effective package could be read to conflict -> the FROZEN PACKAGE CONTROLS and the consumer STOPS. This artifact is a successor derivation, not an amendment, and has no power to override a clause it consumes.
A consumer finds a node satisfied by citing a measurement recorded in this artifact -> that satisfaction is REFUSED, per INV-6.
